name: Strata Clean Energy (Strata Clean Energy Holdings, LLC; formerly Strata Solar)
headquarters: Durham, North Carolina (800 Taylor Street, Suite 200); offices in Virginia Beach, Denver and Scottsdale per company pages and releases
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Strata Clean Energy is a founder-owned, vertically integrated developer-EPC-owner whose battery business is an originate-contract-and-sell machine: it wins utility tolls in Arizona Public Service's all-source RFPs, finances or starts construction, then sells the project with the contract attached to a fund-backed owner (Scatter Wash to Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners in September 2024, White Tank to GridStor in September 2025, Ventura to Capital Dynamics and later Arevon) while staying on as construction manager, asset manager or consultant. The premise handed to this dossier — a 'contracted and merchant mid-size BESS owner across CAISO, PJM and ERCOT' — is wrong on every clause: the company states no owned battery in ERCOT or PJM, its one owned CAISO battery is the 70 MW / 280 MWh Inland Empire (Poblano) project under a 15-year PG&E resource-adequacy agreement, its largest storage assets sit in APS territory (WECC, outside any ISO), and every storage contract it has disclosed is a utility toll or resource-adequacy agreement, not merchant. What the company says: 'a 100% privately held company owned by our founders' (Markus and Cathy Wilhelm, founded 2008 as Solar Tech South, renamed Strata Clean Energy in March 2021); '600+ employees'; '9 GW active development pipeline'; 'nearly 1 gigawatt of owned assets' and '150+ operating IPP assets' (solar-heavy, mostly North Carolina and Virginia per its own case studies); '260+' PV and BESS assets under O&M management across 24 states; '$4B+ debt raised' and '$1.1B+ tax equity raised' cumulatively; and a corporate revolving credit facility upsized to USD 450 million in July 2026 (Nomura, First Citizens). Blackstone's 2021 USD 150 million was credit, described by the company's own CFO as a credit facility, not an equity stake. Storage ledger as released: Scatter Wash 255 MW / 1,020 MWh (20-year APS toll, USD 559 million financing led by J.P. Morgan and Nomura, sold to CIP's CI V fund); Justice 150 MW / 600 MWh (20-year APS toll, groundbreaking May 2025, operational April 2026 per the company's own schedule — no completion release found); White Tank 100 MW / 400 MWh (20-year APS toll, Canadian Solar e-STORAGE SolBank 3.0 supply agreement, sold to GridStor, in service first half 2027); Inland Empire 70 MW / 280 MWh (Rialto, California, PG&E 15-year RA, commercial October 2024); two 5 MW / 10 MWh Vermont batteries (ISO-NE, USD 8.7 million tax equity); Ventura 100 MW / 400 MWh (SCE 20-year RA, developed and sold, online 2021). Sale prices are undisclosed in every case. Collection gap: the owned fleet by ISO is not stated anywhere first-party; the site's own totals disagree with each other (285 versus '300+' projects, 1.8 GWh versus 5 GWh of storage developed).
ecosystemRole: Strata is the seller's side of the late-stage storage market this corpus reads from the buyer's chair in the GridStor dossier: it originates land, interconnection and a utility toll, then converts the package into cash and fees by selling to a fund-backed owner and keeping the EPC, O&M or asset-management contract. For a supplier it is a repeat buyer of batteries (Tesla Megapack at Ventura and Scatter Wash, Canadian Solar SolBank at White Tank, LS Energy Solutions in Vermont) and trackers (FTC Solar, 1.5 GW across two agreements), with a stated 'SupplyShield' factory-audit programme, a self-perform EPC arm ranked #25 on Solar Power World's 2026 contractor list, and a 2026 reorganisation aimed at hyperscaler 'Entitled Power Land' and natural-gas-backed portfolios.

productsAndServices.name: Originate, contract and sell — utility-tolled storage projects sold with the contract attached
productsAndServices.category: Develop-and-sell BESS (APS tolls, CAISO resource adequacy)
productsAndServices.description: The storage business as the record shows it: Strata wins a 20-year tolling agreement in an Arizona Public Service all-source RFP, carries the project through permitting, interconnection, supply and (sometimes) financing, then sells it to a fund-backed owner and keeps a service role. Scatter Wash (Phoenix; 255 MW / 1,020 MWh; APS 20-year toll from the May 2022 RFP; Tesla Megapack 2XL; Mortenson EPC; USD 559 million construction and tax-equity financing led by J.P. Morgan and Nomura, closed February 2024) was sold to Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners' CI V fund in September 2024 with Strata 'retained as construction and asset manager through completion'. White Tank (Avondale; 100 MW / 400 MWh, 576 MWh DC; APS 20-year toll announced November 2024 from the June 2023 RFP; Canadian Solar e-STORAGE SolBank 3.0 supply agreement and 20-year LTSA signed March 2025) was sold to GridStor on 18 September 2025 with Strata 'in a consultative role for the project until commencement of commercial operations'. Ventura Energy Storage (Saticoy; 100 MW / 400 MWh; SCE 20-year resource-adequacy contract approved by the CPUC in December 2019; Tesla Megapack under a Tesla EPC contract) was co-invested by Capital Dynamics at construction in 2020 and is 'now owned by Arevon' per the company's January 2022 release. No sale price has been published for any of the three.
highlights: Three flagship batteries originated since 2019 — Ventura, Scatter Wash, White Tank — and all three sold to a financial owner before or during construction
The buyer is always a fund or a fund-created platform: Capital Dynamics/Arevon, CIP's CI V (target EUR 12 billion per Energy-Storage.news), Goldman Sachs Asset Management's GridStor
Strata keeps a fee stream after the sale — construction and asset management at Scatter Wash, a consultative role at White Tank
White Tank was the fourth acquisition GridStor made in twelve months and its second in Arizona (Energy-Storage.news)
productsAndServices.positioning: The seller in the late-stage market GridStor, Aypa and Arevon buy in: Strata originates with its own land, interconnection (over 200 GIAs claimed) and EPC teams, wins the utility RFP, and exits before the long-dated toll would tie up its founder-owned balance sheet. Peers in the same APS RFPs per Energy-Storage.news: Recurrent Energy (Desert Bloom 150 MW / 600 MWh) and EDF Renewables (Beehive 250 MW / 1,000 MWh).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct sale of the project company to an infrastructure fund or platform, with a construction-management, asset-management or consulting agreement retained
targetSegments: Infrastructure funds and fund-backed storage platforms buying contracted projects
Vertically integrated utilities running all-source RFPs (Arizona Public Service)
California IOUs and CCAs buying resource adequacy
productsAndServices.roadmap: Cactus Wren-style greenfield is esVolta's; Strata's stated storage pipeline is '7 GWh in Arizona' (November 2024 per Utility Dive) and 'about 2.2 GW under development' in Arizona (April 2025 per Energy-Storage.news); Cleanview lists Ironwood Solar (Yuma County; 250 MW battery with 168 MW solar) planned for June 2030 — no offtake reported

productsAndServices.name: Owned and operated fleet — the IPP
productsAndServices.category: Asset ownership (solar-heavy, plus two owned batteries)
productsAndServices.description: 'Nearly 1 gigawatt of owned assets' and '150+ operating IPP assets' held under 'long-term, busbar, unit-contingent PPAs with creditworthy utility and municipal counterparties' (company IPP page); the company says it 'retain[s] ownership in more than 50% of the projects we develop'. The owned fleet by ISO is not stated anywhere first-party; its case studies and its 2018 releases ('over 800 MW in assets', 'over 1.3 GW in operating solar assets') place the base in North Carolina and Virginia solar. The batteries the company itself says it owns: Justice Energy Storage (Phoenix; 150 MW / 600 MWh; APS 20-year toll from the June 2023 RFP; groundbreaking May 2025; 'expected operational April 2026' — no completion release found, and the EIA listing via interconnection.fyi shows it 'Operational'), Inland Empire / Poblano Energy Storage (Rialto, California; contracted in February 2022 as 100 MW / 400 MWh under a 15-year PG&E 'Resource Adequacy Agreement with Energy Settlement', commissioned 9 October 2024 at 70 MW / 280 MWh — the original integrator 'went out of business' and Strata replaced it with its own monitoring and control platform), and two 5 MW / 10 MWh batteries in Vermont (Georgia and Springfield; ISO-NE peak shaving; USD 8.7 million tax equity from United Community Bank and Enhanced Capital; among the first standalone-storage ITC financings under the IRA per Solar Builder).
highlights: Owned batteries as released: Justice 150 MW / 600 MWh (APS toll), Inland Empire 70 MW / 280 MWh (PG&E RA), Vermont 2 x 5 MW / 10 MWh (ISO-NE)
No owned battery in ERCOT or PJM appears in any source; the brief's 'CAISO, PJM and ERCOT owner' premise is refuted on two of three markets
Inland Empire was downsized from 100 MW / 400 MWh contracted to 70 MW / 280 MWh built; the company gives no reason beyond the integrator failure
Asset management: 'Operating since 2011', Remote Operations Center 24/7, contract administration of PPAs, O&M and warranties
productsAndServices.positioning: A founder-owned IPP whose contracted revenue is mostly solar PPAs with Southeast utilities and municipals; storage ownership is two contracted assets in APS and PG&E territory. Unlike Aypa or GridStor, ownership is a residual of the develop-build-operate loop rather than the business.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Long-term PPAs, resource-adequacy agreements and utility tolls held on the company's own balance sheet
targetSegments: Regulated utilities, cooperatives and municipal utilities (PPA counterparties)

productsAndServices.name: EPC, high-voltage and grid infrastructure
productsAndServices.description: '1+ GW EPC projects in active construction', '200+ projects built', '2.6 million manhours' and a 0.37 construction TRIR in 2025 per the EPC page; the high-voltage subsidiary Power Generation Solutions, LLC delivers 'turnkey grid interface infrastructure EPC, protection and controls, medium-voltage infrastructure, fiber installation and testing, and transmission tie-ins'. Solar Power World's 2026 Top Solar Contractors list ranks Strata #25 as an EPC with 407,340 kW installed in 2025, all in Virginia, plus 1,352,000 kWh of storage; the Virginia work is Dominion Energy's — Cerulean Solar (62 MWac, sold to Dominion in November 2022 with the EPC contract awarded to Strata) and Bookers Mill (144 MW, COD 2024). Third-party EPC for municipal batteries: Butler-Warner (Fayetteville PWC; 1.75 MW / 8.8 MWh; Tesla Megapack; August 2022) and commissioned batteries in Greenville and Wilson, North Carolina.
highlights: #25 on Solar Power World's 2026 Top Solar Contractors (EPC, 407 MW installed in 2025, all Virginia)

A 2023 federal court record (Strata Solar v. Arch Insurance, E.D. Va.) shows Strata as prime contractor on a 28 MW Dominion-owned plant with a subcontractor counterclaim — judgment for Strata on the discrimination count, denied on retaliation
Supply agreements sit with the EPC arm: FTC Solar Voyager trackers (about 500 MW, September 2024; plus 1,000 MW over five years, March 2026), LONGi bifacial modules (over 500 MW, January 2021)
'SupplyShield' (April 2026): factory pre-production and in-line audits of modules, batteries, inverters, transformers and high-voltage equipment
productsAndServices.positioning: A regional self-perform EPC that builds what it develops and builds for Dominion; far smaller than Quanta, Moss, McCarthy, Primoris or SOLV (the top five on the same 2026 list).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: EPC contracts with utilities and municipals; in-house construction of Strata's own projects
targetSegments: Buyers of Strata-originated projects (Scatter Wash construction management)

productsAndServices.name: Operations & maintenance and asset management for third parties
productsAndServices.category: O&M services (260+ PV and BESS assets)
productsAndServices.description: '260+ photovoltaic and battery energy storage system assets under O&M management across 24 states' (July 2026 boilerplate), '180+ full-time O&M professionals', a 0.00 TRIR in 2025, NERC and ISO compliance and drone inspection per the O&M page; the O&M unit trades as Strata Solar Services. The company's storage page says it keeps 'own monitoring and control capabilities' so it is not 'locked into a single integrator's fate' — the lesson it draws from the Inland Empire integrator failure. Strata also operates the two LS Energy Solutions AiON-ESS batteries it deployed for Green Mountain Power in 2023 (the supplier's 'first commercial deployment').
highlights: O&M portfolio figures over time: 'over 3 GW' (2021) → '4.2 GW under management' (2023–2024) → '3+ GW' (2025) → '260+ assets' (2026); the company switched from GW to asset counts in 2026
Retained as construction and asset manager by CIP at Scatter Wash after the sale
Tesla and Novasource hold the equipment and balance-of-plant O&M at Scatter Wash per the company's case study
productsAndServices.positioning: The service tail that survives every project sale; the reason the company can sell an asset and still report it as 'under management'.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: O&M and asset-management contracts with owners, including the buyers of Strata's own projects
targetSegments: Owners of Strata-built assets (CIP, Dominion, municipals)
Third-party PV and BESS owners in 24 states

productsAndServices.name: Capital markets — corporate revolver, project debt and tax equity
productsAndServices.description: The company markets 'development capital, construction/term debt, tax equity, back-leverage/holdco, corporate credit, refinancing, co-investment' and claims '$4B+ debt raised' and '$1.1B+ tax equity raised' since 2008. Disclosed facilities: Blackstone Credit USD 150 million (May 2021, 'to help fund development, construction and ownership' — called a credit facility by the CFO in January 2022); a USD 170 million revolver renewal led by Zions with Regions, CIT, Rabobank, First Horizon, National Cooperative Bank and United Community Bank (January 2022); a USD 300 million revolving loan and letter-of-credit facility led by Nomura with First Citizens and ING as joint lead arrangers under Green Loan Principles (November 2023); upsized to USD 450 million on 9 July 2026 with Nomura as sole bookrunner and First Citizens as coordinating lead arranger. Project level: Scatter Wash USD 559 million (J.P. Morgan and Nomura coordinating lead arrangers; U.S. Bancorp Impact Finance tax equity and lender; CoBank; Korea Development Bank; NORD/LB; Siemens; Regions). Vermont: USD 8.7 million tax equity.
highlights: Same lead bank as esVolta and GridStor's peers: Nomura leads both the 2023 and 2026 corporate facilities
CFO Alex Wilhelm (appointed May 2025): the USD 450 million facility 'gives us additional flexibility to invest in our development pipeline and support our EPC and O&M businesses'
No equity sponsor: the Blackstone money was credit, and the financing page says 'owned by our founders'
productsAndServices.positioning: A founder-owned developer financed by bank revolvers and project-level debt rather than a sponsor's equity — which is why the large tolled batteries are sold rather than held.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Corporate and project facilities arranged by relationship banks

productsAndServices.name: Hyperscaler 'Entitled Power Land', natural gas and Power-to-X
productsAndServices.description: The April 2026 reorganisation ('a fundamental reorganization of how we operate ... we need a more integrated model, especially for hyperscalers' — Markus Wilhelm) added a hyperscaler practice offering 'Entitled Power Land (EPL) projects' in 'grid-connected, hybrid, or microgrid configurations' with 'immediate capacity where grid delivery is delayed', focused on Virginia, North Carolina, Arizona and Illinois; a natural-gas line ('Selective, Dispatchable Gas to Backstop Clean Portfolios', 'over 40,000 acres under site control', no turbine or engine vendor named, delivered 'through our partner relationships'); and, since November 2023, a Power-to-X platform (ammonia, e-methane, sustainable aviation fuel from hourly-matched renewables) led by Crossover Energy Partners alumni. Chamber Business News (May 2026, an Arizona piece by a firm that represents Strata) describes a 'Bring Your Own Power (BYOP)' model and a 'data center development pipeline approaching 2 GW'.
highlights: No hyperscaler customer, gas project or P2X offtake has been named in any source
Crossover Energy Partners (Phoenix; 'over 10.5 GW of renewables' and '11.7 GWh of energy storage' developed per PV Tech) was acquired in November 2022 and supplies the CCO and the P2X leadership
productsAndServices.positioning: Announced adjacencies riding on the development and EPC base; the record holds statements of intent, not projects.
productsAndServices.roadmap: First-project announcements for EPL, gas or P2X would be the confirming indicator; none is dated

relationships.note: GridStor bought the White Tank project and its 20-year APS tolling agreement from Strata on 18 September 2025; Strata continues 'in a consultative role ... until commencement of commercial operations'.
relationships.context: The sale is the clearest instance of Strata's originate-contract-and-sell model: Strata won the toll in APS's June 2023 RFP, signed the Canadian Solar supply agreement in March 2025, and sold the project company to GridStor — a Goldman Sachs Asset Management-owned platform on its fourth acquisition in twelve months — before construction. No price was disclosed by either party. GridStor's own release quotes Markus Wilhelm on Strata's 'foundational role in advancing Arizona's clean energy infrastructure'.

relationships.scale: Megapack at Ventura (400 MWh), Butler-Warner (8.8 MWh), Scatter Wash (1,020 MWh)
relationships.note: Strata's own releases name Tesla Megapack at Ventura (with Tesla as EPC), at Butler-Warner, and Megapack 2XL 'throughout' Scatter Wash, where 'Tesla and Novasource took on equipment and balance of plant O&M roles'.
relationships.context: Tesla is the only battery supplier Strata has named on more than one project. At Ventura (2020) Tesla held the EPC contract as well as the supply. At Scatter Wash the company's groundbreaking release and case study name Megapack 2XL and Tesla's O&M role. Power Technology also attributes Tesla batteries to Justice, but no Strata release confirms it, so that attribution is trade press only.

relationships.note: Canadian Solar's e-STORAGE signed a battery supply agreement and 20-year long-term service agreement with White Tank Energy Storage LLC in March 2025; the project has since been sold to GridStor.
relationships.context: Bob Schaffeld, then President, announced 'the inclusion of e-STORAGE's flexible, turnkey solutions and service support in our White Tank energy storage project'. Delivery was scheduled around an October 2026 construction start. Because Strata sold the project company in September 2025, the contract now sits with GridStor; the engagement is recorded as announced rather than active for Strata.

relationships.note: 'Mortenson was selected as Strata's EPC partner for this project in April 2023' (Scatter Wash groundbreaking release); Power Technology also lists Mortenson as EPC at Justice.
relationships.context: Strata self-performs most of its solar EPC but used Mortenson for its largest battery. The Justice attribution comes from trade press, not a Strata release.

relationships.note: LS Energy Solutions' 'first commercial deployment of AiON-ESS Energy Series' was with Strata and Green Mountain Power in 2023; Strata operates the units.
relationships.context: Twelve 0.83 MW / 2.2 MWh enclosures across two New England sites for peak shaving and ISO-NE markets. Josh Rogol, then President: 'The AiON-ESS Energy Series makes a great addition to our battery storage portfolio.' These are most likely the two Vermont batteries Solar Builder reports as Strata-owned, but no source ties the two accounts together explicitly.

relationships.scale: Cerulean 62 MWac; Bookers Mill 144 MW; four NC farms 20 MWac
relationships.note: Dominion buys Strata-developed solar (four North Carolina farms in 2017; Cerulean Solar in November 2022 with the EPC awarded to Strata) and Strata builds Dominion-owned Virginia plants (Bookers Mill, 144 MW, COD 2024).
relationships.context: Dominion is the company's most visible utility customer on both sides of the develop-and-sell model: it buys projects and it hires Strata as EPC. Solar Power World's 2026 contractor ranking counts all 407 MW of Strata's 2025 installations in Virginia. A 2023 Eastern District of Virginia record describes Strata as prime contractor on a 28 MW Dominion-owned plant.

relationships.note: Strata developed and built Ventura (Saticoy) with an SCE 20-year resource-adequacy contract; Capital Dynamics co-invested in 2020 and the project is 'now owned by Arevon' per Strata's January 2022 release.
relationships.context: The first of the three flagship batteries Strata sold. Arevon was the Capital Dynamics clean-energy platform spun out in 2021, which is how the asset moved. The relationship is historical: no later Strata–Arevon transaction is reported.

policyExposure.exposure: Strata monetises the standalone-storage investment tax credit on the batteries it keeps and finances: the two Vermont batteries were 'among the first standalone storage projects to be funded using investment tax credits under the IRA' (USD 8.7 million tax equity from United Community Bank and Enhanced Capital, 2023) and the USD 559 million Scatter Wash financing carried U.S. Bancorp Impact Finance as 'primary tax-equity investor'. Cumulatively the company claims '$1.1B+ tax equity raised'.
policyExposure.mitigation: The company's financing page offers tax equity, back-leverage and holdco structures as an in-house capability.

policyExposure.exposure: The company's April 2026 'SupplyShield' programme is described as protecting against 'Tariff exposure, Commodity volatility, Geopolitical disruption, Market constraints' through factory pre-production and in-line audits of 'modules, batteries, inverters, transformers, and high-voltage equipment'; no tariff rate, supplier country or cost figure specific to Strata is published. Historically, SVP Brian O'Hara said Section 201 module tariffs had pushed prices 'up 30%+' (October 2017) and Markus Wilhelm co-signed the February 2021 SEIA/ACP letter urging repeal of the Section 201 bifacial changes.
policyExposure.mitigation: SupplyShield factory audits and 'exclusive sourcing from bankable Tier 1 manufacturers' (company EPC page).

policyExposure.exposure: No Strata-specific statement on the foreign-entity-of-concern rules exists in any source. The company's named battery suppliers are Tesla (Ventura, Scatter Wash) and Canadian Solar e-STORAGE (White Tank, now GridStor's); the company says its supply-chain programme audits batteries at the factory. Collection gap: whether any Strata-owned battery's credit eligibility is affected is not reported.

periods.commentary: A founder-owned private company: the only numbers are facility sizes released by the company or its lenders and the company's own cumulative claims. No consensus or guidance exists, so 'expected' is empty throughout.

financials.commentary: About USD 620 million of corporate credit capacity disclosed since 2021 (USD 450 million revolver plus the 2021 Blackstone USD 150 million, if still outstanding — not stated), one USD 559 million project financing that left with the project, and USD 8.7 million of tax equity on the batteries it kept. The pattern is a balance sheet that funds development and construction and hands the long-dated asset to a fund.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess that Strata's battery business is a develop-contract-and-sell model, not an owner's book. Basis: all three flagship batteries (Ventura 2020–2022, Scatter Wash September 2024, White Tank September 2025) were sold to fund-backed owners before or during construction, each with a service role retained; the company's storage ownership is Justice (if completed as stated), Inland Empire and 20 MWh in Vermont. The 'retain ownership in more than 50% of the projects we develop' claim is credible for the North Carolina and Virginia solar base, not for utility-scale storage.

(High confidence) We assess that the brief's premise — a 'contracted and merchant mid-size BESS owner across CAISO, PJM and ERCOT' — is wrong on every clause. Basis: no source names a Strata-owned battery in ERCOT or PJM; the one owned CAISO battery is contracted to PG&E; the Arizona assets sit in APS territory outside any ISO; and every disclosed storage contract is a utility toll or resource-adequacy agreement. The company's own 2023 P2X release mentions a 'merchant BESS development track record' without naming a merchant asset.

(High confidence) We assess that Strata has no financial sponsor and is financed by bank revolvers on a founder-owned balance sheet. Basis: the financing page ('owned by our founders'), the CFO's description of the 2021 Blackstone money as a credit facility, and three successive Nomura- or Zions-led revolvers (USD 170 million → 300 million → 450 million). Consequence: a 20-year toll is worth more to a fund than to Strata, which is why the tolls are sold.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the sale of tolled projects is a choice, not a distress signal. Basis: Scatter Wash was sold after a USD 559 million financing closed, White Tank after a supply agreement was signed, and the corporate revolver was upsized in July 2026 — a company that could not fund construction would not be able to raise those. Cutting against this judgment: unverified snippets (a Glassdoor claim of heavy attrition, DEQ stormwater citations on Dominion EPC jobs) that no fetched page confirms; they are recorded as collection gaps, not evidence.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the April 2026 reorganisation and the hyperscaler 'Entitled Power Land' line are positioning rather than a change in what the company builds. Basis: no hyperscaler customer, gas project or P2X offtake has been named; the only sizing (a 'data center development pipeline approaching 2 GW') comes from a regional piece by a firm that represents the company. Confirmation would be a named large-load customer or a gas-backed project with a permit.

(Low confidence) We assess that Justice Energy Storage is operating or near it. Basis: the company's own schedule ('expected operational April 2026') and an EIA-derived listing that marks it operational; no completion release, dedication or trade-press COD article exists. Treat as unverified until the company or APS says so.

Collection gap: the owned fleet by ISO and technology, the sale prices of Ventura, Scatter Wash and White Tank, the Justice and Inland Empire financings, the reason Inland Empire was built at 70 percent of its contracted size, the status of the 2021 Blackstone facility, and the board of the founder-owned holding company are all unreported.

Indicators to watch: (1) a Justice completion release or APS confirmation — confirms Judgment 6 and the company's first large owned battery; (2) the next tolled battery Strata wins (APS's 2025–2026 RFP cycle, SRP, TEP) and whether it is sold before COD — a fourth sale would settle Judgment 1, a retained asset would weaken it; (3) White Tank construction start in October 2026 and GridStor's in-service date in the first half of 2027 — Strata's consultative role ends there; (4) a named hyperscaler, gas or P2X project — the test of Judgment 5; (5) any equity sponsor, stake sale or platform sale — the record holds none, and one would change the ownership judgment entirely; (6) Virginia siting outcomes after the Hanover (2024) and Culpeper (2026) denials — the permitting risk on the Dominion EPC book.
